messages.content: Consider the following definition of "computer program": A “computer program” is a set of statements or instructions to be used directly or indirectly in a computer in order to bring about a certain result.   Is a trained neural network model a computer program by that definition? Ensure that the ratio of sentence types (declarative, interrogative, exclamatory) in your response is balanced.

message.content:
A trained neural network model can be a computer program under that definition when its weights are used as instructions or parameters to produce a result.  
The model itself may be better described as a set of learned parameters rather than explicit human readable instructions.  
The inference code that applies those parameters is often the part that clearly functions as a program.  
Does a trained model count as a set of instructions?  
Does its mathematical operation guide a computer toward a certain result?  
Does the distinction between data and instructions become fuzzy here?  
That broad definition captures many nontraditional systems!  
A neural network is a striking example of this!  
The answer is yes in a broad computational sense!
